short: A Judaean revolt against Roman rule ended with the Temple destroyed and the province devastated.
full:
Resentment over taxation, Roman mismanagement and religious friction boiled over in 66 CE when Judaean rebels overran the Roman garrison in Jerusalem and destroyed a relief force under the Syrian legate Cestius Gallus. Nero dispatched the general Vespasian, who methodically reconquered Galilee and the countryside over the following two years while Judaean factions fought increasingly bitter internal battles inside Jerusalem itself.

Vespasian's elevation to emperor in 69 left the siege of Jerusalem to his son Titus, who took the city in 70 after a prolonged blockade, destroying the Second Temple. Resistance continued at isolated fortresses, most famously Masada, which fell around 73. The war killed a substantial part of Judaea's population, ended Temple-centred Jewish worship, and financed the Flavian dynasty's building programme in Rome through plundered wealth and captives.
